messages:
marta: heads up — after last canary the per-route latency chart is way slower (3-4x). FCP fine, chart rendering stalls while waiting on fetches :eyes:
liam: which chart exactly? query id or sample window changed?
marta: the `/api/console/metrics/route-latency` series. Canary bumped `sample_size` from 100 -> 1000 in the rollout config. repro: open /routes, click timeline, network shows repeated `GET /metrics/route-latency?sample=1000` and hung promises
noah: hmm we also pushed a routing policy change that routes telemetry reads through the metrics-proxy for quota enforcement — could add ~150-300ms per request under load
arjun: that + 10x sample size is a bad combo. continuous batching for chart queries collapses into many concurrent long requests. do we have any caching on the proxy for preaggregates?
marta: proxy has a 1s in-memory TTL for preaggregates, but the client explicitly passes `cache-control: no-cache` when sample>500 (this was added in the rollout)
liam: why is client forcing no-cache for large samples? that was intended for debug only, not default. looks like the rollout config mis-applied the flag to production routes :facepalm:
console-bot: deploy 2165432000 to service/console-client completed by liam — release notes: "increase sample window + debug cache bypass flag"
noah: ok root cause seems clear: (1) sample_size increase -> N larger requests, (2) client-side cache-bypass set for >500, (3) metrics-proxy added hop. Combined causes chart stalls and bundle perceived slowness because UI awaits payloads
arjun: quick mitigation: revert the cache-bypass, and limit sample_size to 200 for the canary cohort. also add a heuristic to use preaggregates endpoint for UI sampling.
marta: agreed. can we patch the client config and re-deploy only the config flag? that should restore cached responses immediately
liam: I'll roll back the cache-bypass flag now and reduce sample_size for canary. rolling back in 2 mins. @console-bot please monitor errors/latency for /metrics/route-latency
console-bot: alerting rule updated: monitor(service:metrics, endpoint:/metrics/route-latency, p95>400ms) — notifications to #incidents and @oncall
marta: after rollback i still see some inflight requests stuck in the browser tab. clearing the prefix cache helped for me. might need a small client patch to avoid sending stale concurrent fetches when sample_size toggles
liam: noted, follow-up PR to debounce sample requests during config flip. will create after rollback
noah: also let's add a test in the telemetry e2e that simulates sample window growth and ensures we hit preaggregate cache path not cold-read path
arjun: agree. putting a temporary guard in the proxy to respect preaggregate key even if `cache-control` present for UI-origin requests would buy time
marta: thanks — watching metrics. will post a small gif of the timeline once numbers drop :thumbsup:
liam: rollback done. p95 dropped from ~720ms -> ~140ms in the canary orgs already :tada:
marta: confirmed, charts responsive again. follow-ups: debounce client, e2e test, proxy guard. I'll open tickets and assign owners
noah: assign me the proxy guard, liam take the client debounce, arjun you own the e2e?
arjun: on it.
marta: perfect. closing thread when PRs are up.
